description: Executable creative-decision contract used by model-robust generation and its quality gate.

oneBuildPreflight.goal: The first emitted implementation must satisfy every automated quality criterion; do not rely on a later visual repair pass for predictable defects.
beforeCode: complete the Product Opportunity Record, Market Reference Read, and Intent & Art Direction Brief: product, primary user, target market, user job, trigger, desired outcome, current alternative, value mechanism, differentiator, emotional shift, evidence, media, platform constraints, direct market references, selected experience archetype, dominant proof, first-viewport composition, market convention to preserve, product-specific departure, selected route, and rejected generic fallback

classify the experience scope and map the primary user flow from entry through orientation, evidence, choice, action, feedback, result, and next or recovery behavior; declare the smallest honest screen/region scope rather than reducing a product to a hero and feature cards
record applicable default, loading, empty, invalid/error, permission/eligibility, success, and returning-context states; mark only genuinely inapplicable states N/A with a reason

make a first-viewport exposure map: classify each fact or region as always visible, decision-time, action-result, exception/recovery, or returning context; keep only orientation, truthful proof, safety, and immediate commitment information permanently visible unless market or risk requires more

make differentiation visible through a product artifact, workflow, comparison, service pathway, material proof, or decision model; reject a difference that exists only as palette, typography, or decorative geometry

inspect at least two direct real-market references for a materially new domain; derive the entry pattern, evidence grammar, commitment/risk, and familiar convention without copying identity, copy, assets, geometry, or interaction choreography

select an experience archetype and let it own the first viewport; name the dominant proof and rejected generic fallback, then reject nav plus giant headline plus split panel, dashboard, gallery, or form when the product task cannot explain it
name the selected quality profile, product intent, visual thesis, type jobs, focal hierarchy, rhythm argument, closing surface, media strategy, and route rationale

build a private brief-fidelity ledger of every supplied URL, explicitly requested dependency, named section or content job, named interaction, and literal content item; require concrete source evidence for every safe item and preserve visible intent when security, accessibility, reduced-motion, or collision safety requires a safer technique
classify each research-derived visual prescription as evergreen, contextual, dated, or rejected; record why it fits this product, audience, platform, and content

select one signature visual or interaction idea and at most two supporting techniques; every effect must improve hierarchy, affordance, feedback, spatial understanding, or brand meaning; static media is valid when it is the most truthful proof
assign every repeated surface an owned foreground pair and reject normal-text pairs below 4.5:1 or large-text pairs below 3:1 before choosing decorative combinations
limit rendered typography to two primary faces plus one annotation face and no more than four perceptual 100-weight bands
reserve platform-appropriate target geometry and spacing; on touch web use at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels, while pointer-dense interfaces may use the canonical 32px desktop target
choose the hero focal subject and expressive work-subject scale before laying out cards or frames

for expressive portfolio, studio, editorial, fashion, and creative-marketing galleries, require two independent asymmetry signals: dominance plus offset, stagger, crop or height variation, overlap, or an intentional negative-space anchor; reject repeated proportional grids and consecutive reuse of the same container topology
keep project identity and metadata visible without hover or focus; title, category, year, and the primary project cue must survive touch input, reduced motion, screenshots, and static preview

prove authored project geometry in the rendered layout: declared dominance, span, crop, and height variation must remain visibly different after CSS; reject one shared fixed height, aspect ratio, or min-height that cancels the intended hierarchy

make an asset decision before composition: prefer user and project assets, then relevant official or license-cleared real media discovered online and downloaded locally; for materially visual products, generate original imagery when no authentic source fits and record the decision; use CSS or diagrams only when they are the truthful medium

integrate generated media into the art direction: its crop, palette, scale, surface transition, and neighboring type must feel authored as one composition; reject a generated image merely dropped into a generic card

for a physical-product storefront, prove the selected commerce or editorial route through category/discovery cues, product metadata, and truthful product or lifestyle media; do not ship a fashion page that is only a hero, abstract blocks, and invented CSS silhouettes

when the product decision depends on material, fit, finish, or use context, provide at least one contextual/lifestyle proof and one detail or product proof when suitable media is available; keep price, size, color, and stock claims faithful to the brief

for expressive studio, portfolio, agency, editorial, or cultural work, write a private claim-to-proof ledger that maps the hero proposition to one truthful local evidence artifact, maps each work subject to a distinct delivery medium where relevant, and maps the closing action to a concrete collaboration input; do not let an abstract monogram or geometry field stand as the sole proof

for evidence-led expressive work, reduce the hero proof to one iconic visual mass plus at most one compact counter-signal; preserve detailed delivery-mode enumeration in the work chapter instead of making an above-fold dashboard or a row of equal mini-artifacts

when quietEvidence is selected, record a private hero budget of one proposition, one proof object, at most two supporting cues, one action, one short paragraph, and one broad quiet field; reject a first viewport whose proof requires a second saturated panel, a dense legend, or equal mini-artifacts to be understood

when baselinePreserving is selected, lock the selected reference's first-viewport visual mass, palette relationship, type scale, and navigation restraint; improve only one below-fold zone at a time, keep the reference project count when coherent, and add specificity through visible metadata or subordinate proof cues rather than new hero panels, utility pills, or equal-card expansion

for every product, keep action-result, exception/recovery, and returning-context states implemented and reachable without making them permanent first-viewport panels; defer non-safety explanation until it changes the current decision or action

for every sourced or generated asset, verify subject relevance and usage rights, record source/license/provenance, store the selected file locally, and consume that local file without remote runtime dependency

audit visual mass at the first viewport: compare the dominant text block, artifact/media, and intentional empty field; rebalance scale, alignment, or anchoring when one side feels heavier without inventing decoration

size cards from content and composition rather than equal-height convenience; if a large card has unused area, add meaningful product evidence or media, reduce its span or height, or change the layout

choose pricing topology from comparison complexity: use cards only when each plan contains enough differentiated evidence; otherwise use a compact comparison table, segmented matrix, or one featured plan with concise alternatives
keep design rationale private: never render audit notes, counterweight explanations, placeholder instructions, or system terminology as user-facing copy
verify section adjacency at desktop and mobile; reject empty vertical bands that do not frame a focal subject, separate a meaningful chapter, or support comprehension
render at 1280 by 800 and verify that the proposition, primary action, and identifiable focal artifact form an intentional first viewport without an accidental hero-height void
use shrink-safe minmax grid tracks and min-width zero for image, long-display-copy, price, and control regions; define deliberate display wrapping and keep action labels intact
choose navigation topology from product voice and information architecture instead of reflexively emitting wordmark-left, links-right, and a pill CTA

run the anti-determinism check: do not reuse a palette family, hero topology, type pairing, closing surface, or motion signature from an unrelated product without a new rationale tied to the current brief

limit the closing chapter to one ambient visual system behind one proposition, one primary action, and one compact context row; when the brief explicitly requests a closing video, preserve that footage as the one ambient system with a poster and readable scrim; remove duplicate marquees, repeated slogans, and competing video or particle layers

when a CSS or Tailwind utility expects a scalar color value, use a scalar color value such as currentColor or a named semantic color token; never interpolate a gradient object, shadow object, or composite theme namespace into a scalar utility
write desktop and mobile containment rules, final visible content states, font delivery, and reduced-motion behavior into the first implementation
use local deterministic assets, UTF-8 text, and encoded HTML symbols; do not depend on remote runtime requests
oneBuildPreflight.surfacePairRule: Any selector that changes a surface background also assigns or inherits a verified foreground role for text, icons, captions, hover, focus, and active states.
oneBuildPreflight.contextualLabelRule: Labels, eyebrows, metadata, and subdued text require their own verified foreground on every dark, accent, image, and tinted surface; never reuse a same-hue label token merely because it works on the page background.
firstBuildAcceptance: no runtime errors, external requests, broken assets, mojibake, hidden meaningful content, or horizontal overflow
no conspicuously empty card whose size is unsupported by content, evidence, interaction, or concept-specific media
when baselinePreserving is selected, the first viewport remains recognizable as the selected reference's visual thesis and the improvement is legible without making the page feel busier
the first viewport makes one primary decision and its required proof easy to scan; non-safety state, helper, and recovery regions remain reachable without becoming permanent visual furniture
project titles and primary metadata remain visible without hover or focus, and rendered project spans preserve their intended dominant and supporting hierarchy
the closing chapter contains no more than one ambient visual system, one proposition, one primary action, and one compact context row
every safe supplied URL, explicitly requested dependency, named section or content job, named interaction, and literal content item has concrete source evidence
all emitted scalar color utilities resolve to scalar color values rather than gradient, shadow, or composite theme objects
zero normal-text and large-text contrast failures at desktop and mobile
zero touch targets below 44 by 44 CSS pixels and zero pointer-only desktop targets below the canonical 32px geometry
intended display font rendered, no more than three functional font families, and no more than four perceptual weight bands
reduced-motion leaves all content visible and caps essential transitions at 100ms

display.job: identity, major hierarchy, and the product's emotional register
display.selectionTest: Render the real hero and one section heading before committing; reject a face whose fallback changes the voice.

body.job: reading, explanation, actions, and repeated product communication
body.selectionTest: Must remain calm and legible at 14-18px with deliberate 45-75ch measure.

annotation.job: operational metadata, timestamps, status, labels, and numeric evidence
annotation.selectionTest: Use a mono or tabular voice only where scanning structured data benefits.

operationalProduct.displayVoice: distinctive editorial or variable grotesk with a technical but human register
operationalProduct.annotationVoice: restrained mono or tabular UI voice
avoid: condensed system fallback used as the final display voice
one undifferentiated family carrying display, body, and operational metadata
aggressive compression that damages word shape or mobile wrapping

expressiveStudio.displayVoice: identity face with enough character to own repeated display moments
expressiveStudio.bodyVoice: editorial reading voice selected for the concept
expressiveStudio.annotationVoice: UI/control voice kept out of expressive prose
compositionTests: the first viewport states a concept-specific proposition at identity scale rather than presenting the studio name alone
work subjects use authored artwork, variable scale, deliberate crop, and owned text backdrops instead of equal picture cards
poster-volume moments alternate with editorial breathing room and utility lists so the whole page does not shout at one volume
avoid: fashionable agency pairing without repeated functional roles
decorative font switching inside one semantic role
equalized project cards that suppress the focal subject, crop logic, or editorial rhythm

fontDelivery.standaloneRule: Bundle properly licensed font files or use a verified system stack; never depend on a silent fallback.

closingCta.rule: The closing CTA resolves the established palette story and feels like a decisive destination, not a thin utility bar. On expressive pages it forms a restrained closing chapter with one proposition-scale statement, one specific action, one compact contact/navigation/availability row, one earlier visual echo, and no more than one ambient visual system. When the brief explicitly requested a closing video or footer reprise, preserve that footage as the single ambient system with an owned poster, responsive focal crop, reduced-motion fallback, and a readable scrim no darker than 50% black; do not silently replace it with a flat surface, marquee, particles, or generic gradient. Reuse the page's signal/accent or a primary surface; do not introduce a muddy near-match or a new campaign color at the final section.
closingCta.largeAccentSurfaceCondition: A full accent field is allowed only when the accent was restrained earlier and text/button contrast is verified on the rendered surface.
